title: Natural local Hom cohomology from a bounded finite free resolution
statement: Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an open, B an O_Y-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and E an integer cochain complex of O_U-modules [def-pur-hom-complex], bounded above AND below with finite free terms. Let epsilon:E -> (B|U)[0] be a quasi-isomorphism. Fix any integer q and any supplied ambient derived category [def-pc-derived-category]. The functor C -> H^q(RHom_Y(B,C))|U [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is naturally isomorphic to C -> H^q(Hom_U(E,(C|U)[0])). The conclusion is a natural isomorphism on the whole category of coefficient sheaves, with no closed immersion, affine chart, Koszul sequence, or quotient coefficient specified. No derived category on U in the supplied universe is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 20.46.9, finite locally free Hom comparison, with Tag 08DL for restriction

proof.text: Specialize the existing functorial derivedInternalHom_comparison to the fixed single complex B[0] and all coefficient single complexes. Whisker with derived homology and exact restriction. Use the homology factorization and the exact restriction homology comparison, followed by the natural ordinary Hom restriction isomorphism, to identify the left coefficient functor with C |-> H^q Hom_U(Rc(B[0]),Rc(I(C[0]))).

Restriction to the over-U site preserves K-injectives; the over-site equivalence does also, as a right adjoint to its exact inverse. Transport this property through overFunctorEquiv. Precomposition with epsilon, transported by the single/restriction comparison, is therefore a natural quasi-isomorphism on Hom into these restricted coefficient resolutions. Whisker with homology to obtain a natural isomorphism.

Whisker the natural coefficient resolution map with restriction and Hom(E,-). Exact restriction preserves its quasi-isomorphism, and bounded finite free Hom preserves that quasi-isomorphism without requiring a target bound. After homology this natural transformation is an isomorphism. Invert it, compose the preceding comparisons, and finish with the single/restriction natural isomorphism. No derived category on U is used.

theorem local_finite_free_homology_natural
    {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (U : Y.Opens) (B : Y.Modules)
    (E : CochainComplex U.toScheme.Modules ℤ)
    (hbounded : ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ p : ℤ, N < p → IsZero (E.X p))
    (hbelow : ∃ M : ℤ, ∀ p : ℤ, p < M → IsZero (E.X p))
    (hfree : ∀ p : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (E.X p ≅
      SheafOfModules.free (R := moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace)
        (ULift.{u} (Fin r))))
    (ε : E ⟶ (CochainComplex.singleFunctor U.toScheme.Modules 0).obj
      ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).obj B)) [QuasiIso ε] (q : ℤ) :
    let S := DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    Nonempty (S ⋙ (Functor.curry.obj H).obj (op (S.obj B)) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) q ⋙
        Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι ≅
      Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι ⋙
        CochainComplex.singleFunctor U.toScheme.Modules 0 ⋙
        (homComplexFunctor (R := U.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf)).obj (op E) ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor U.toScheme.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℤ) q)
